scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that leans toward consensus while insisting ideals must guide it; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Politics constantly forces a choice between chasing a perfect vision and making a workable deal.
Some claim the goal of politics should be the pursuit of an ideal, while others argue it should be finding common ground and reasonable consensus.
I lean toward seeking consensus, but I believe ideals must still guide the search for it.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why consensus is the wiser goal

sentences.text: First, finding common ground is often the only way to make government actually work.
In a divided society, no single group can have everything it wants, so compromise becomes necessary.
For example, an important law usually passes only when opposing sides agree to give something up.
This shows that reasonable consensus can turn endless conflict into real progress.
Leaders who chase only a perfect ideal often achieve nothing but anger and deadlock.
Working toward agreement also helps hold a divided nation peacefully together.
For these reasons, I lean toward consensus as the wiser goal.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why ideals must still guide it

sentences.text: Second, however, the pursuit of ideals should not be abandoned in the search for agreement.
Ideals give politics its direction and remind leaders what they are really trying to achieve.
Consider reformers who refused to compromise on justice and changed unfair laws most people once accepted.
Such courage shows that some ideals are worth defending even when easy agreement is impossible.
A politics of pure compromise can drift without purpose, settling for far too little.
Real progress sometimes requires holding firm to a principle until others can be won over.
Both views, then, capture something politics must somehow hold together.
In conclusion, I believe the goal of politics should usually be reasonable consensus.
But ideals must still guide that search, or compromise loses all direction.
The best politics seeks common ground while staying true to the ideals worth pursuing.
